open_issues: The reader set is 1 token under its new budget, so any future reader edit needs another budget decision.
The study verifier is 1 token under its budget, and the study producer is 4 under.
docs/records.md and crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs are listed as deliverables but I left them unchanged.
The spec's 'Run: cargo test -p athena-core verify' was not run as written. I ran the athena-core tests as part of a larger command, and the verify tests passed.
mistakes: I first wrote a stray scratch file into docs/ (decisions.md.tail) and removed it right after. It is not in the diff.
I first cited the new record as D90, which was already used. I fixed every reference to D93.
My first verifier trim removed phrases a test pins, and the test failed. I restored them.
I did not edit crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs or docs/records.md. The budgets test needed no change, and records.md has no budget mention.
D93's 'Why removals cannot pay' paragraph is a judgment argument. It rests on the budgets test's measured counts and on the producer and verifier trims, which show removals did work for those roles.
learnings: The budgets test checks all three roles, so the added reader, producer and verifier text needed matching trims in the producer and verifier prompts to stay inside their unchanged budgets (study producer 1,096/1,100, study verifier 1,299/1,300).

A unit test in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs pins exact phrases in the verifier frame, including 'say so explicitly in evidence and findings' and 'never report it as a result on the real repository', so those cannot be shortened.
D90 to D92 were already taken in docs/decisions.md, so the new record is D93.
The defaults-loop.md line 47 mention of the budget sat inside a very long table row, so I edited it by exact substring.
The token count is ceil(bytes/3.0), a prose tripwire rather than the live count.
